To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
earthworms can be used as a bioresource for the valorization of fermented tannery solid wastes.

the vermicompost obtained from hydrolysed ANFL treated by E. eugeniae showed a significant reduction of heavy metals, total carbon and an increase of total Kjeldahl nitrogen as compared to untreated waste, and the vermicomposted extracts showed no phytotoxicty on selected commercial crops.
the combination of hydrolysis and vermicompost is a good alternative for the management of ANFL waste.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valorisation of a solid waste generated in the leather processing industry through a low-cost and environmentally friendly process, and the production of a valuable organic fertilizer.
the utilization of the fermented ANFL by earthworm E. eugeniae for the production of a value added compost, which could be used for the growth of different commercial crops.
the utilization of a solid waste generated during leather processing by using a sustainable approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the earthworms are able to utilize and transform fermented tannery waste into a value-added organic fertilizer with improved physico-chemical and enzymatic properties.
the earthworms can effectively utilize and transform the solid wastes into a value added compost within a short residence time of 25 days.
the earthworms are able to transform the fermented ANF in the SSF and SmF into a value added compost with improved nutritional quality and reduced phytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of ANFL fermentation and vermicast is a good alternative for the management of this solid waste.
the earthworms can be used for the treatment of tannery waste and the treated waste could be used as a fertilizer.

the vermicompost obtained by the combination of both treatments (fermentation and vermicompost) could be a promising source of organic fertilizer for agricultural use and could be used for improving the growth of tomato, green gram, and cucumber.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the earthworms are capable of transforming the fermented ANFL into a value added organic fertilizer with a high potential for agricultural application.
the earthworms have a positive effect on the quality of the vermicompost and its use for agricultural purposes.
the vermicompost can be utilized as a soil amendment to improve the soil fertility and crop productivity.
